# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Casey Iverson
**Member ID:** W207784190
**Plan:** Fidelis Care (Commercial/ACA), New York
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-25
**Reference number:** POC-1ACF427871-17933
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Musculoskeletal Surgery (https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf)

Dear Fidelis Care Appeals Department,

I am writing to request reconsideration of the denial of my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which was denied in the notice dated 2026-08-25, reference number POC-1ACF427871-17933. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to review this decision again.

**A note on the criteria used in this review**

The clinical criteria provided to me in connection with this denial are drawn from the section of the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines - Musculoskeletal Surgery covering cervical spine fusion procedures, such as Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) and Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion (CPDF). For example, one of these criteria states:

> "○ Upper extremity weakness ○ Unsteady gait related to myelopathy/balance or generalized lower extremity weakness ○ Disturbance with coordination ○ Hyperreflexia ○ Hoffmann sign ○ Positive Babinski sign and/or clonus ● Progressive neurological deficit (motor deficit, bowel or bladder dysfunction) with corresponding evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on an MRI or CT scan images – immediate surgical evaluation is indicated When ALL of the following criteria are met (6–8):"

This language, and the other cervical fusion criteria referenced in connection with my denial, concern neck and spinal cord conditions. My requested procedure is a partial knee replacement, not a cervical spine surgery, and I do not have neck or spine symptoms. I do not believe these criteria are the correct standard by which my knee surgery should have been evaluated, and I am asking the plan to confirm that the correct medical necessity criteria for CPT 27446 were applied to my case.

I have not been given, and therefore cannot quote, the plan's specific medical necessity criteria for partial knee replacement. I am asking that my case be reviewed under whatever criteria the plan actually applies to CPT 27446, and I am setting out below the clinical facts that I believe support medical necessity under any reasonable standard for this procedure.

**Summary of my clinical history**

- I have had progressive knee pain for 24 months that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-05-14 through 2026-07-09) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI of my knee on 2026-07-30 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially.
- I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times per night due to pain.
- On exam, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

Given this history — including a documented, severe structural finding on MRI (bone-on-bone, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) and a documented trial of conservative treatment (physical therapy, medication, and injection) that did not provide lasting relief — I believe the imaging and clinical record do support the medical necessity of this surgery. My surgeon has reviewed this same record and has recommended the procedure.

**What I am asking**

I ask that the plan:

1. Confirm which specific medical necessity criteria for partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) were used to reach this denial, since the criteria referenced to me concern cervical spine fusion and do not appear to apply to my knee condition; and
2. Reconsider the denial in light of the clinical record summarized above, including the MRI findings, the completed course of physical therapy, medication trial, and injection, and my surgeon's recommendation.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-21. I will submit this appeal using the address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I can also find the appeal or grievance form for my state at ambetterhealth.com, or call the number on my member ID card with questions.

Please let me know if any additional records or forms are needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

[Casey Iverson]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

[Date]
